verdict.rationale: Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol has agents sign every request with RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures (aligned with web-bot-auth). Signatures carry interaction tags, timestamps and nonces for replay protection, and merchants verify them against Visa's published JWKS keys. The open reference implementation includes an agent-registry and a cdn-proxy verifier, explicitly built so merchants can distinguish credentialed agents from anonymous bots. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration that merchant-side signature verification works in production (the probe only confirms the spec and repo are published), and no evidence of graded trust tiers beyond the binary legitimate-or-not signal.
